target_paper_title: Physics-Driven Spatiotemporal Modeling for AI-Generated Video Detection

related_work_items.paper_title: Demamba: Ai-generated video detection on million-scale genvideo benchmark

evidence.evidence_text: Ma et al. [39] and Chen et al. [25] propose Transformer-and mamba-based frameworks to model spatiotemporal relationships in video frame features for detection.
We compare our NSG-VD with following baselines: TALL [24], NPR [27], STIL [36], and Demamba [25].
For instance, Demamba struggles with generative paradigms like HotShot (40.60% Recall) and Sora (48.21% Recall).

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: Demamba is a main direct comparator on the same AI-generated video detection task, and the paper uses its weaker results on difficult generators to motivate the need for physics-driven modeling beyond learned spatiotemporal feature modeling.

related_work_items.paper_title: Tall: Thumbnail layout for deepfake video detection

evidence.evidence_text: Xu et al. [24] transform consecutive frames into a predefined layout via masking/resizing to enable efficient spatiotemporal modeling.
We compare our NSG-VD with following baselines: TALL [24], NPR [27], STIL [36], and Demamba [25].
TALL fails on synthetic outliers (e.g., 25.00% Recall on Sora).

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: TALL is a direct baseline for video forgery detection, but the paper presents it as another conventional spatiotemporal modeling approach that remains vulnerable on highly realistic generated videos.

related_work_items.paper_title: Spatiotemporal inconsistency learning for deepfake video detection

evidence.evidence_text: Gu et al. [36] separately model spatial and temporal inconsistencies, and introduce a vertical slicing feature fusion mechanism to establish a more comprehensive spatial-temporal representation.
We compare our NSG-VD with following baselines: TALL [24], NPR [27], STIL [36], and Demamba [25].
STIL collapses completely on critical cases (e.g., 1.40% Recall on HotShot and 1.79% Recall on Sora), revealing limitations of their inherent dependencies on generator-specific artifacts.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: STIL is explicitly compared in experiments and helps define the paper's gap: modeling inconsistency cues alone is not robust enough when generated videos become highly realistic and artifact cues weaken.

evidence.evidence_text: Traditional methods [22,23,24] often rely on specific artifacts like appearance consistency and optical flow-based motion modeling, struggling with highly realistic content yet physically implausible.
Bai et al. [38] fuse frame-level and optical flow predictions to detect spatial-temporal anomalies.

Existing AI-generated video detection methods primarily rely on local feature inconsistencies (e.g., optical flow-based motion modeling [22], appearance consistency modeling [23]) ... However, they often ignore physics-driven constraints governing spatiotemporal evolution inherent to natural videos.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: The optical-flow detection line is a key foil for the paper's framing because NSG-VD is presented as replacing artifact-specific motion cues with a physics-grounded statistic over probability flow.

related_work_items.paper_title: Altfreezing for more general video face forgery detection

evidence.evidence_text: Wang et al. [23] propose an alternating-freezing strategy with spatiotemporal augmentation for facial consistency modeling.
While most methods utilize facial priors, their reliance on domain-specific features limits their generalizability to more general AI-generated content detection.
Existing AI-generated video detection methods primarily rely on local feature inconsistencies ... or supervised learning with large-scale datasets [25,24,26,27].

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: AltFreezing represents the face-forgery-specific appearance-consistency line that the paper argues does not generalize well to general AI-generated video detection.

related_work_items.paper_title: Detecting machine-generated texts by multi-population aware optimization for maximum mean discrepancy

evidence.section: Exploring NSG for Detecting AI-Generated Videos
evidence.evidence_text: Recent studies show Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) [33]-a non-parametric statistic for distribution alignment-has demonstrated remarkable capabilities in measuring distributional differences, e.g., AI-text detection [48,46] and adversarial samples detection [57,58].
Considering the multiple-population scenarios across diverse video distributions [48], we adopt a multi-population aware optimization for the kernel training.

Note that while MMD is conventionally used for distribution-level comparisons, recent studies [48, 46, 58] validate its efficacy in single-sample detection by quantifying deviations from reference distributions.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: This paper is a bridge from MMD-based machine-generated text detection to the target paper's video setting, especially for the multi-population-aware kernel optimization adopted in NSG-VD.
